'''Marius Nicolae Crainic''' ({{IPA|ro|ˈmari.us nikoˈla.e ˈkrajnik}}; February 3, 1973, [[Aiud]]) is a [[Romania]]n mathematician working in the [[Netherlands]].

==Education and career==
Born in [[Aiud]], Romania, Crainic competed in the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]] of 1990 receiving a Bronze medal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imo-official.org/results/contestant/2484/|title=Marius Crainic|website=[[International Mathematical Olympiad]]}}</ref> He obtained a bachelor's degree at [[Babeș-Bolyai University]] ([[Cluj-Napoca]]) in 1995. He then moved to the Netherlands and obtained a master's degree in 1996 at [[Radboud University Nijmegen|Nijmegen University]]. He received his [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in 2000 from [[Utrecht University]] under the supervision of [[Ieke Moerdijk]]. His Ph.D. thesis is titled "''Cyclic cohomology and characteristic classes for foliations''".<ref name=":0">{{MathGenealogy|id=69260}}</ref>

He was a [[Miller Research Fellows|Miller Research Fellow]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://miller.berkeley.edu/images/newsletters/2003_spring.pdf |title=Miller Institute News |access-date=2020-02-02}}</ref> at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 2001 to 2002. He then returned to Utrecht University as a Fellow of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (KNAW). In 2007 he became an associate professor at Utrecht University, and since 2012 he is a full professor. In 2016 he was elected member of KNAW.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/12165|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200517164100/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/members/12165|title=Crainic, Prof. dr. M.N. (Marius) — KNAW|website=www.knaw.nl|archive-date=2020-05-17}}</ref>

In 2008 Crainic was awarded the [[André Lichnerowicz Prize|André Lichnerowicz Prize in Poisson Geometry]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lpthe.jussieu.fr/~dito/poissongeometry/index.php?page=lichne|title=Poisson Geometry Home Page|website=www.lpthe.jussieu.fr|access-date=2020-01-30}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://euro-math-soc.eu/andr%C3%A9-lichneriwicz-prize-henrique-bursztyn-and-marius-crainic|title=The André Lichneriwicz prize to Henrique Bursztyn and Marius Crainic|website=euro-math-soc.eu|language=en|access-date=2020-02-01}}</ref> and in 2016 he received the [[Nicolaas Govert de Bruijn|De Bruijn]] Prize.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uu.nl/en/news/mathematician-prof-marius-crainic-receives-first-de-bruijn-prize|title=Mathematician Prof. Marius Crainic receives first De Bruijn Prize|date=2017-09-21|website=Utrecht University|language=en|access-date=2020-01-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nieuwarchief.nl/serie5/pdf/naw5-2016-17-2-105.pdf |title=Laudation for Marius Crainic |access-date=2020-02-02}}</ref> In 2026 he was awarded the Dutch Mathematics Prize for his pioneering work in the field of Poisson geometry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Dutch Mathematics Prize . |url=https://kwg.nl/en/prijs/de-nederlandse-wiskundeprijs/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |language=en|website=[[Koninklijk Wiskundig Genootschap]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Marius Crainic receives the first Dutch Mathematics Prize . |url=https://platformwiskunde.nl/en/2026/06/marius-crainic-ontvangt-eerste-nederlandse-wiskundeprijs/ |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=Platform Wiskunde Nederland |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Marius Crainic receives first Dutch Mathematics Prize |url=https://www.uu.nl/en/news/marius-crainic-receives-first-dutch-mathematics-prize |access-date=2026-07-04 |website=[[Universiteit Utrecht]]}}</ref>

In July 2020 he was an invited speaker to the 8th [[European Congress of Mathematics|European congress of Mathematics]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=8th European Congress of Mathematics|url=https://www.8ecm.si/program/invited-speakers|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2020-02-01|website=8th European Congress of Mathematics}}</ref> which has been rescheduled to 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=8th European Congress of Mathematics – 2020 rescheduled to June 2021|url=https://www.8ecm.si/news/68|access-date=2020-10-12|website=8th European Congress of Mathematics}}</ref>

==Research==
Crainic's research interests lie in the field of [[differential geometry]] and its interactions with [[topology]]. Differential Geom.]]|volume=66|issue=1|pages=71–137|doi=10.4310/jdg/1090415030|year=2004|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0210152}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crainic|first1=Marius|last2=Mǎrcuţ|first2=Ioan|title=A normal form theorem around symplectic leaves|journal=[[J. Among his most well-known results are a solution to the long-standing problem of describing the obstructions to the integrability of [[Lie algebroid|Lie algebroids]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crainic|first1=Marius|last2=Fernandes|first2=Rui|date=2003-03-01|title=Integrability of Lie brackets|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=157|issue=2|pages=575–620|doi=10.4007/annals.2003.157.575|issn=0003-486X|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0105033}}</ref> and a new geometric proof of Conn's linearization theorem,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crainic|first1=Marius|last2=Fernandes|first2=Rui Loja|date=2011-03-01|title=A geometric approach to Conn's linearization theorem|journal=Annals of Mathematics|volume=173|issue=2|pages=1121–1139|doi=10.4007/annals.2011.173.2.14|issn=0003-486X|doi-access=free|arxiv=0812.3060}}</ref> both written in collaboration with [[Rui Loja Fernandes]], as well as the development of the theory of [[representation up to homotopy|representations up to homotopy]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crainic|first1=Marius|last2=Abad|first2=Camilo Arias|date=2011-06-17|title=Representations up to homotopy of Lie algebroids|journal=[[Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik]]|volume=2012|issue=663|pages=91–126|doi=10.1515/CRELLE.2011.095|hdl=1874/234207 |s2cid=18662057|issn=0075-4102|url=https://www.zora.uzh.ch/id/eprint/58213/1/_j_crll_ahead-of-print_crelle_2011_095_crelle_2011_095_pdf.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crainic|first1=Marius|last2=Abad|first2=Camilo Arias|title= The Weil algebra and the Van Est isomorphism|journal=[[Annales de l'Institut Fourier]]|volume=61 (2011)|issue=3|pages=927–970|doi=10.5802/aif.2633|year=2011|doi-access=free|arxiv=0901.0322}}</ref>

He is the author of more than 40 research papers in peer-reviewed journals<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.nl/citations?user=HSmygYcAAAAJ|title=Marius Crainic - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.nl|access-date=2020-02-01}}</ref> and has supervised 13 PhD students as of 2025.<ref name=":0" />
